243: **[SECTION 12 --- DATA DELETION]{.underline}**
244: 
245: **12.1** Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement for any reason, the Processor shall, at the Controller\'s choice and subject to Section 12.2, delete all Personal Data Processed on behalf of the Controller, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof, within ninety (90) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration of the Agreement. Deletion shall be performed using industry-standard secure deletion methods that render the Personal Data unrecoverable, including, where applicable, cryptographic erasure, multi-pass overwriting, or physical destruction of storage media.
246: 
247: **12.2** Notwithstanding Section 12.1, the Processor may retain Personal Data to the extent and for the duration required by European Union or German federal or state law to which the Processor is subject, including without limitation any mandatory data retention obligations under German commercial law (*Handelsgesetzbuch*) or German tax law (*Abgabenordnung*). In such cases, the Processor shall promptly inform the Controller of the applicable legal requirement and the categories of Personal Data to be retained, and shall limit its Processing of the retained Personal Data strictly to the purposes required by such law. The Processor shall ensure that retained Personal Data is subject to the confidentiality and security obligations set forth in this DPA for the duration of its retention.
248: 
249: **12.3** Upon request by the Controller following the completion of deletion under Section 12.1, the Processor shall provide written confirmation of the deletion of the Controller\'s Personal Data, signed by an authorized officer of the Processor. Such confirmation shall specify the date of deletion, the categories of data deleted, and the deletion methods used. The Processor shall provide such confirmation within thirty (30) calendar days of the Controller\'s request.
250: 
251: **12.4** The Controller acknowledges that deletion of Personal Data from the Processor\'s backup systems may require additional time beyond the ninety (90) calendar day period specified in Section 12.1 due to the Processor\'s automated backup rotation cycles. In such cases, the Processor shall ensure that all Personal Data is deleted from backup systems within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration, and shall isolate and restrict access to such backup copies pending their deletion.
252: 
253: **[SECTION 13 --- LIABILITY]{.underline}**
254: 
255: **13.1** The Processor\'s aggregate liability for all claims of any kind arising under or in connection with this DPA, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed five hundred thousand Euros (€500,000). This limitation applies to the aggregate of all claims arising under or in connection with this DPA, regardless of the number of events, incidents, or claims giving rise to such liability.
256: 
257: **13.2** In no event shall the Processor be liable for any indirect, incidental, consequential, special, punitive, or exemplary damages arising out of or related to this DPA, including but not limited to loss of revenue, loss of profits, loss of business or anticipated savings, loss of goodwill, loss of data or corruption of data, or cost of procurement of substitute services, regardless of the theory of liability and even if the Processor has been advised of the possibility of such damages or should have foreseen the possibility thereof. This exclusion of consequential damages shall apply to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.
258: 
259: **13.3** The limitations and exclusions set forth in this Section 13 shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and shall survive the termination or expiration of this DPA. The Parties acknowledge that the limitations and exclusions set forth in this Section 13 reflect a fair and reasonable allocation of risk between the Parties, taking into account the nature of the Services, the fees payable under the Agreement, and the respective responsibilities of the Parties under this DPA and applicable law.
260: 
261: **13.4** Nothing in this Section 13 shall limit the Processor\'s liability for damages caused by a failure to comply with its obligations under the GDPR specifically directed to processors, or for damages caused to Data Subjects arising from the Processor\'s non-compliance with its obligations under Article 82 of the GDPR. Article 82 of the GDPR provides that any processor involved in processing shall be liable for damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with obligations of the GDPR specifically directed to processors, or where it has acted outside of or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller.
262: 
263: **13.5** For the avoidance of doubt, each Party shall be liable for the entirety of the damage suffered by a Data Subject in accordance with Article 82(4) of the GDPR, subject to any right of recourse between the Parties as provided in Article 82(5) of the GDPR. Where a Party has paid full compensation for the damage suffered, that Party shall be entitled to claim back from the other Party that part of the compensation corresponding to the other Party\'s share of responsibility for the damage.
264: 
265: **[SECTION 14 --- GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**
266: 
267: **14.1** This DPA and any disputes arising out of or in connection with this DPA, including disputes regarding the existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination of this DPA, and including any non-contractual claims arising out of or in connection with this DPA, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. To the extent that the GDPR or other mandatory provisions of European Union law apply to any matter arising under this DPA, such provisions shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions of German national law.
268: 
269: **14.2** Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this DPA that the Parties are unable to resolve through good-faith negotiations within thirty (30) calendar days of one Party\'s written notice to the other Party describing the nature of the dispute and the relief sought, shall be finally settled by arbitration administered by the Deutsche Institution für Schiedsgerichtsbarkeit e.V. (\"DIS\") in accordance with the DIS Arbitration Rules (DIS-Schiedsgerichtsordnung) in effect at the time of the commencement of the arbitration proceedings. The seat of arbitration shall be Munich, Germany. The language of the arbitration proceedings shall be English. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three (3) arbitrators, with each Party nominating one arbitrator and the two Party-nominated arbitrators selecting the presiding arbitrator. If the two Party-nominated arbitrators fail to agree on the selection of the presiding arbitrator within thirty (30) calendar days of the appointment of the second Party-nominated arbitrator, the presiding arbitrator shall be appointed by the DIS Appointing Authority in accordance with the DIS Arbitration Rules.
270: 
271: **14.3** The arbitral tribunal shall have the authority to award any remedy or relief that a court of competent jurisdiction could grant, including but not limited to monetary damages, declaratory relief, and specific performance, provided that the arbitral tribunal shall not have the authority to award punitive or exemplary damages except to the extent that such damages are recoverable under Article 82 of the GDPR or other mandatory provisions of applicable law.
272: 
273: **14.4** Nothing in this Section 14 shall prevent either Party from seeking interim, provisional, or injunctive relief from any court of competent jurisdiction, including courts in Germany or any other jurisdiction, where such relief is necessary to prevent irreparable harm or to preserve the status quo pending the resolution of a dispute through arbitration. Any application for interim or injunctive relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the right to arbitrate.
274: 
275: **14.5** All arbitration proceedings and any arbitral award shall be kept strictly confidential by the Parties and the arbitrators, except to the extent that disclosure is required by applicable law, by a Supervisory Authority, or in connection with the enforcement of an arbitral award.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Processor may update Annex B (Technical and Organizational Measures) from time to time in accordance with Section 5.5 of this DPA.

lines.text: **[SECTION 12 --- DATA DELETION]{.underline}**

**12.1** Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement for any reason, the Processor shall, at the Controller\'s choice and subject to Section 12.2, delete all Personal Data Processed on behalf of the Controller, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof, within ninety (90) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration of the Agreement. Deletion shall be performed using industry-standard secure deletion methods that render the Personal Data unrecoverable, including, where applicable, cryptographic erasure, multi-pass overwriting, or physical destruction of storage media.

**12.2** Notwithstanding Section 12.1, the Processor may retain Personal Data to the extent and for the duration required by European Union or German federal or state law to which the Processor is subject, including without limitation any mandatory data retention obligations under German commercial law (*Handelsgesetzbuch*) or German tax law (*Abgabenordnung*). In such cases, the Processor shall promptly inform the Controller of the applicable legal requirement and the categories of Personal Data to be retained, and shall limit its Processing of the retained Personal Data strictly to the purposes required by such law. The Processor shall ensure that retained Personal Data is subject to the confidentiality and security obligations set forth in this DPA for the duration of its retention.

**12.3** Upon request by the Controller following the completion of deletion under Section 12.1, the Processor shall provide written confirmation of the deletion of the Controller\'s Personal Data, signed by an authorized officer of the Processor. Such confirmation shall specify the date of deletion, the categories of data deleted, and the deletion methods used. The Processor shall provide such confirmation within thirty (30) calendar days of the Controller\'s request.

**12.4** The Controller acknowledges that deletion of Personal Data from the Processor\'s backup systems may require additional time beyond the ninety (90) calendar day period specified in Section 12.1 due to the Processor\'s automated backup rotation cycles. In such cases, the Processor shall ensure that all Personal Data is deleted from backup systems within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days of the effective date of termination or expiration, and shall isolate and restrict access to such backup copies pending their deletion.
**[SECTION 13 --- LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**13.1** The Processor\'s aggregate liability for all claims of any kind arising under or in connection with this DPA, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed five hundred thousand Euros (€500,000). This limitation applies to the aggregate of all claims arising under or in connection with this DPA, regardless of the number of events, incidents, or claims giving rise to such liability.

**13.2** In no event shall the Processor be liable for any indirect, incidental, consequential, special, punitive, or exemplary damages arising out of or related to this DPA, including but not limited to loss of revenue, loss of profits, loss of business or anticipated savings, loss of goodwill, loss of data or corruption of data, or cost of procurement of substitute services, regardless of the theory of liability and even if the Processor has been advised of the possibility of such damages or should have foreseen the possibility thereof. This exclusion of consequential damages shall apply to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.

**13.3** The limitations and exclusions set forth in this Section 13 shall apply to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and shall survive the termination or expiration of this DPA. The Parties acknowledge that the limitations and exclusions set forth in this Section 13 reflect a fair and reasonable allocation of risk between the Parties, taking into account the nature of the Services, the fees payable under the Agreement, and the respective responsibilities of the Parties under this DPA and applicable law.

**13.4** Nothing in this Section 13 shall limit the Processor\'s liability for damages caused by a failure to comply with its obligations under the GDPR specifically directed to processors, or for damages caused to Data Subjects arising from the Processor\'s non-compliance with its obligations under Article 82 of the GDPR. Article 82 of the GDPR provides that any processor involved in processing shall be liable for damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with obligations of the GDPR specifically directed to processors, or where it has acted outside of or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller.

**13.5** For the avoidance of doubt, each Party shall be liable for the entirety of the damage suffered by a Data Subject in accordance with Article 82(4) of the GDPR, subject to any right of recourse between the Parties as provided in Article 82(5) of the GDPR. Where a Party has paid full compensation for the damage suffered, that Party shall be entitled to claim back from the other Party that part of the compensation corresponding to the other Party\'s share of responsibility for the damage.
**[SECTION 14 --- GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**

**14.1** This DPA and any disputes arising out of or in connection with this DPA, including disputes regarding the existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination of this DPA, and including any non-contractual claims arising out of or in connection with this DPA, shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. To the extent that the GDPR or other mandatory provisions of European Union law apply to any matter arising under this DPA, such provisions shall prevail over any inconsistent provisions of German national law.

**14.2** Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this DPA that the Parties are unable to resolve through good-faith negotiations within thirty (30) calendar days of one Party\'s written notice to the other Party describing the nature of the dispute and the relief sought, shall be finally settled by arbitration administered by the Deutsche Institution für Schiedsgerichtsbarkeit e.V. (\"DIS\") in accordance with the DIS Arbitration Rules (DIS-Schiedsgerichtsordnung) in effect at the time of the commencement of the arbitration proceedings. The seat of arbitration shall be Munich, Germany. The language of the arbitration proceedings shall be English. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three (3) arbitrators, with each Party nominating one arbitrator and the two Party-nominated arbitrators selecting the presiding arbitrator. If the two Party-nominated arbitrators fail to agree on the selection of the presiding arbitrator within thirty (30) calendar days of the appointment of the second Party-nominated arbitrator, the presiding arbitrator shall be appointed by the DIS Appointing Authority in accordance with the DIS Arbitration Rules.

**14.3** The arbitral tribunal shall have the authority to award any remedy or relief that a court of competent jurisdiction could grant, including but not limited to monetary damages, declaratory relief, and specific performance, provided that the arbitral tribunal shall not have the authority to award punitive or exemplary damages except to the extent that such damages are recoverable under Article 82 of the GDPR or other mandatory provisions of applicable law.

**14.4** Nothing in this Section 14 shall prevent either Party from seeking interim, provisional, or injunctive relief from any court of competent jurisdiction, including courts in Germany or any other jurisdiction, where such relief is necessary to prevent irreparable harm or to preserve the status quo pending the resolution of a dispute through arbitration. Any application for interim or injunctive relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the right to arbitrate.

**14.5** All arbitration proceedings and any arbitral award shall be kept strictly confidential by the Parties and the arbitrators, except to the extent that disclosure is required by applicable law, by a Supervisory Authority, or in connection with the enforcement of an arbitral award.

**16.1** This DPA shall become effective on the date of its execution by both Parties (the \"Effective Date\") and shall remain in full force and effect for the duration of the Agreement, including any renewals, extensions, or amendments thereof, for so long as the Processor Processes Personal Data on behalf of the Controller.

**16.2** This DPA shall automatically terminate upon the termination or expiration of the Agreement, subject to the survival provisions set forth in Section 16.3 below and the Processor\'s obligations under Section 12 (Data Deletion).

**16.3** Notwithstanding the termination or expiration of this DPA, the following provisions shall survive and remain in full force and effect for a period of two (2) years following the effective date of termination or expiration:

**16.4** The survival period specified in Section 16.3 shall commence on the effective date of termination or expiration of this DPA. Upon the expiration of the survival period, the surviving provisions shall cease to have effect, except to the extent that applicable law requires continued compliance with any obligation set forth therein.
**16.5** The provisions of Section 4 (Confidentiality) shall survive the termination or expiration of this DPA indefinitely in accordance with Section 4.3.
**[SECTION 17 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**17.1 Entire Agreement.** This DPA, together with its Annexes and the Agreement, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, understandings, negotiations, and discussions, whether oral or written, between the Parties relating to the Processing of Personal Data in connection with the Services.

**17.2 Amendments.** No amendment, modification, or supplement to this DPA shall be effective unless it is in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Processor may update Annex B (Technical and Organizational Measures) from time to time in accordance with Section 5.5 of this DPA.

**17.3 Severability.** If any provision of this DPA is found by a court or other tribunal of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal, and enforceable, and the remaining provisions of this DPA shall continue in full force and effect. If such modification is not possible, the invalid provision shall be severed and the remaining provisions shall be interpreted so as to give effect to the Parties\' original intent to the maximum extent possible.

**17.4 Waiver.** No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right, power, or privilege under this DPA shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right, power, or privilege preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, or privilege.

**17.5 Notices.** All notices, requests, demands, and other communications required or permitted under this DPA shall be in writing and shall be delivered by hand, by internationally recognized overnight courier service, or by email to the addresses specified in this DPA or such other addresses as a Party may designate in writing from time to time. Notices shall be deemed received upon actual receipt.

**17.6 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign or transfer this DPA, or any of its rights or obligations hereunder, without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that either Party may assign this DPA to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, provided that the assignee agrees in writing to be bound by the terms of this DPA.

**17.7 Counterparts.** This DPA may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this DPA by electronic signature or by exchange of PDF copies shall have the same force and effect as execution and delivery of an original signed counterpart.

The Processing shall be carried out for the duration of the Agreement, including any renewals or extensions thereof, and shall continue until the deletion or return of all Personal Data by the Processor in accordance with Section 12 of the DPA.
**A.5 Nature of Processing**
The Processing includes the following operations performed on Personal Data in connection with the Services:
> • Collection and ingestion of Personal Data from the Controller\'s systems into the Processor\'s cloud infrastructure
> • Storage and hosting of Personal Data in the Processor\'s data centers
> • Recording, organization, and structuring of Personal Data within managed databases
> • Retrieval and consultation of Personal Data in response to authorized queries from the Controller\'s applications

> • Disclosure by transmission of Personal Data between the Processor\'s data centers (Frankfurt, Dublin, and Northern Virginia) for purposes of redundancy, disaster recovery, and load balancing

The purposes of the Processing are to enable the Controller to use the Processor\'s cloud hosting, managed database, and analytics services for the Controller\'s healthcare platform operations, including without limitation:

> • Providing managed database services for the Controller\'s operational and clinical databases
> • Providing disaster recovery and business continuity services to ensure the availability and resilience of the Controller\'s systems
> • Providing anonymized analytics and reporting services to support the Controller\'s operational and clinical decision-making

> • **Patients of the Controller:** Individuals who receive or have received healthcare services from the Controller or the Controller\'s affiliated healthcare providers, and whose Personal Data is stored in the Controller\'s patient management and electronic health records systems hosted by the Processor.

> • **Healthcare provider contacts of the Controller:** Physicians, nurses, specialists, and other healthcare professionals who interact with the Controller\'s systems, including their professional credentials, contact information, and affiliations.

> • **Employees of the Controller:** Employees of the Controller to the extent that their Personal Data is Processed in connection with the Services, including employment-related information stored in systems hosted by the Processor.

The following categories of Personal Data are Processed:

> • Dates of birth
> • Contact information, including email addresses, telephone numbers, and postal addresses
> • Health insurance identifiers and policy numbers
> • Medical record numbers and patient identification numbers

Personal Data is transferred on a continuous, ongoing basis for the duration of the Agreement. Data transfers occur in real time or near-real time as part of the Processor\'s cloud hosting and managed database services.

245: **FLAG FOR LEGAL REVIEW --- Anonymization vs. Pseudonymization :** Data sent to Orionis for \"anonymization\" is personal data at the point of transfer and must be protected accordingly under the GDPR. The critical question is whether Orionis\'s output constitutes truly anonymized data (which would fall outside the scope of the GDPR) or pseudonymized data (which remains personal data subject to the full panoply of GDPR obligations).

247: The DPA must be amended to address this issue comprehensively. Specifically, the DPA should:

249: > \(1\) Define the anonymization standard by reference to objective and verifiable criteria, including the three-criteria test established in WP29 Opinion 05/2014 (WP216): (a) singling out --- it should not be possible to isolate an individual from the dataset; (b) linkability --- it should not be possible to link records relating to the same individual across datasets; and (c) inference --- it should not be possible to deduce information about an individual from the data with significant probability.
250: >
251: > \(2\) Require Orionis to validate and certify that its outputs meet the defined anonymization standard, with such validation to be documented and made available to Pinnacle EU B.V. upon request.

Module 3 must be separately executed between Stratosphere (as Processor/data exporter) and Larkfield (as Subprocessor/data importer), with Pinnacle EU B.V. designated as the Controller with enforceable third-party beneficiary rights under the SCCs. This remote access constitutes an international transfer under the GDPR. No transfer mechanism is specified, referenced, or contemplated in the DPA Template for this scenario. lines.text: **Purpose:** Anonymization and analytics services as described in the DPA Template.

**Nature of Transfer:** This is an intra-EEA transfer from Germany/Ireland to Ireland. Both the data exporter (Stratosphere, Frankfurt/Dublin) and the data importer (Orionis, Dublin) are located within the European Economic Area. No GDPR Chapter V international transfer mechanism is required.

**FLAG FOR LEGAL REVIEW --- Anonymization vs. Pseudonymization :** Data sent to Orionis for \"anonymization\" is personal data at the point of transfer and must be protected accordingly under the GDPR. The critical question is whether Orionis\'s output constitutes truly anonymized data (which would fall outside the scope of the GDPR) or pseudonymized data (which remains personal data subject to the full panoply of GDPR obligations).
The DPA must be amended to address this issue comprehensively. Specifically, the DPA should:

> \(1\) Define the anonymization standard by reference to objective and verifiable criteria, including the three-criteria test established in WP29 Opinion 05/2014 (WP216): (a) singling out --- it should not be possible to isolate an individual from the dataset; (b) linkability --- it should not be possible to link records relating to the same individual across datasets; and (c) inference --- it should not be possible to deduce information about an individual from the data with significant probability.
> \(2\) Require Orionis to validate and certify that its outputs meet the defined anonymization standard, with such validation to be documented and made available to Pinnacle EU B.V. upon request.

> \(3\) Specify that if Orionis\'s outputs do not meet the defined anonymization standard, those outputs shall be treated as \"Personal Data\" under the DPA and shall remain subject to all DPA obligations, including security measures, data retention limits, data subject rights facilitation, breach notification, and, if transferred outside the EEA at any future point, international transfer mechanisms.

> \(4\) Address whether the analytics processing performed on data prior to the completion of the anonymization process constitutes a separate processing activity requiring its own documentation of lawful basis and purpose limitation under Articles 5(1)(b) and 6 GDPR.
**[Section 4: Summary of International Transfers Requiring Legal Mechanisms]{.underline}**

The following table consolidates all data flows identified in Section 3, with particular focus on cross-border transfers requiring a legal mechanism under GDPR Chapter V. For each transfer, the table identifies the exporter, importer, their respective roles, the destination country, the transfer mechanism currently referenced in the DPA Template, the required mechanism, and whether a gap has been identified.

**\#**   **Transfer Description**                                          **Exporter**                                         **Importer**                                     **Exporter Role**             **Importer Role**                  **Destination**           **Mechanism in DPA**    **Required Mechanism**                                       **Gap?**

1        EU data: Pinnacle EU → Stratosphere Frankfurt/Dublin              Pinnacle EU B.V.                                     Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH                 Controller                    Processor                          Germany / Ireland (EEA)   N/A (intra-EEA)         None required                                                No

2        EU data: Stratosphere Frankfurt → Larkfield N. Virginia (DR/BC)   Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH                     Larkfield Data Systems, LLC                      Processor                     Subprocessor                       United States             SCC Module 2 (C-to-P)   **SCC Module 3 (P-to-SP)** + TIA                             **Yes ---/**

3        EU data: Singapore remote access to Frankfurt/Dublin              Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH (Singapore staff)   N/A (remote access)                              Processor personnel           ---                                Singapore                 **Not addressed**       SCCs or other Ch. V mechanism + supplementary measures       **Yes ---**

4        EU data: Stratosphere Frankfurt/Dublin → Orionis Dublin           Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH                     Orionis Analytics Ltd.                           Processor                     Subprocessor                       Ireland (EEA)             N/A (intra-EEA)         None required (but anonymization standard must be defined)   **Partially ---**

5        US data: Pinnacle US → Larkfield N. Virginia                      Pinnacle Health Solutions, Inc.                      Larkfield Data Systems, LLC (via Stratosphere)   Controller / Covered Entity   Subprocessor / BA sub-contractor   United States             N/A (domestic US)       HIPAA BAA flow-down required                                 No international transfer gap
**Key Observations:**

**Larkfield DPF Certification Status.** Larkfield Data Systems, LLC is **NOT** certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (adequacy decision adopted by the European Commission on July 10, 2023). Accordingly, the DPF adequacy decision cannot serve as an alternative or supplementary transfer mechanism for Transfer #2. The only viable mechanism for Transfer #2 is the execution of properly completed SCCs under Module 3 (Processor-to-Subprocessor), accompanied by a Transfer Impact Assessment and appropriate supplementary measures.

**Absence of Transfer Impact Assessment.** No Transfer Impact Assessment is referenced, required, or documented anywhere in the DPA Template for any of the identified international transfers. This applies to both Transfer #2 (Frankfurt to Northern Virginia) and Transfer #3 (Singapore remote access to Frankfurt/Dublin). Post-Schrems II, a TIA is a prerequisite for reliance on SCCs as a transfer mechanism.

**Incorrect SCC Module Selection.** The DPA Template references Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 and attaches only Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) SCCs. While Module 2 may be appropriate for the direct Controller-to-Processor relationship between Pinnacle EU B.V. and Stratosphere (although that relationship does not involve an international transfer), it is not appropriate for the Processor-to-Subprocessor transfer between Stratosphere and Larkfield. Module 3 (Processor-to-Subprocessor) must be separately executed for Transfer #2, with Pinnacle EU B.V. designated as the Controller with enforceable third-party beneficiary rights.
**[Section 5: Data Volume and Regulatory Applicability Summary]{.underline}**

The following table summarizes the data subject populations, approximate data volumes, applicable regulatory frameworks, primary storage locations, and key regulatory notes for each data category involved in the processing relationship.

EU Healthcare Providers               \~320                           GDPR                                                              Frankfurt (DE), Dublin (IE)     Standard personal data; legitimate interest or contractual necessity likely sufficient

US Patients (PHI)                     \~2.1 million                   HIPAA (45 CFR Parts 160, 164); applicable state privacy laws      Northern Virginia (Larkfield)   PHI --- BAA required; Stratosphere is Business Associate; Larkfield is BA sub-contractor

US Healthcare Providers               \~14,000                        Applicable state privacy laws; contractual obligations            Northern Virginia (Larkfield)   Professional contact data; standard contractual protections apply

California Residents (subset of US)   \~890,000                       CCPA/CPRA (Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100 et seq.)                     Northern Virginia (Larkfield)   Service Provider obligations under CCPA/CPRA apply to Stratosphere and Larkfield; restrictions on sale/sharing of PI

**Financial Context:** The MSA annual fees total \$4.2 million, allocated as \$2.8 million for US services and \$1.4 million for EU services. This financial context is relevant to the proportionality assessment for liability cap negotiations addressed in the separate compliance gap memorandum.

**Timeline Note:** The EU expansion launch date is **September 1, 2025**. The DPA must be fully negotiated, executed, and compliant with all applicable GDPR requirements --- including valid international transfer mechanisms for all identified cross-border data flows --- before this date. The internal review deadline for the DPA Template is **May 16, 2025**, which allows approximately four months for negotiation and finalization prior to the launch date.
**[Section 6: Observations and Flags for Legal Review]{.underline}**

This section provides a consolidated list of all issues identified through the data flow mapping exercise described in this document. Each issue is cross-referenced to the relevant DPA Template section, the data flow diagram(s) in which the issue was identified, and the internal issue tracking reference. These flags are intended for use by the legal team in preparing the compliance gap memorandum and DPA redline.
**1. International Transfer --- Wrong SCC Module (Critical)**

The Processor-to-Subprocessor transfer from Stratosphere (Frankfurt data center) to Larkfield (Northern Virginia data center) for disaster recovery and business continuity purposes requires **SCC Module 3 (Processor-to-Subprocessor)** under Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914. The DPA Template (Section 7) references and attaches only Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor), which is legally insufficient for this transfer scenario. Module 3 must be separately executed between Stratosphere (as Processor/data exporter) and Larkfield (as Subprocessor/data importer), with Pinnacle EU B.V. designated as the Controller with enforceable third-party beneficiary rights under the SCCs. Without the correct Module 3 SCCs in place, there is no valid legal mechanism for this transfer under GDPR Chapter V. *See Diagram 3 (Section 3.3) and Summary Table (Section 4), Transfer #2.*.
**2. International Transfer --- Singapore Remote Access Not Covered (High)**

Stratosphere support engineers based in Singapore access EU personal data stored at the Frankfurt and Dublin data centers on a regular basis for incident resolution and technical support. This remote access constitutes an international transfer under the GDPR. No transfer mechanism is specified, referenced, or contemplated in the DPA Template for this scenario. DPA Section 7 is entirely silent on Singapore. The DPA must include a valid GDPR Chapter V mechanism (most likely Module 2 SCCs with Singapore-specific supplementary measures) or Stratosphere must contractually commit to restricting EU data access to EEA-based personnel exclusively. *See Diagram 4 (Section 3.4) and Summary Table (Section 4), Transfer #3.* \[References: \]
**3. International Transfer --- Larkfield Not DPF-Certified (High)**

Larkfield Data Systems, LLC is not certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. The DPF adequacy decision (adopted July 10, 2023) cannot be relied upon as an alternative or supplementary transfer mechanism for any data flows involving Larkfield as the data importer. SCCs under Module 3, accompanied by supplementary measures and a Transfer Impact Assessment, are required. Pinnacle should also consider requesting that Larkfield obtain DPF certification prior to the September 1, 2025 go-live date as an additional protective measure. *See Section 1.3.1, Diagram 3 (Section 3.3), and Summary Table (Section 4), Transfer #2.* \[References: \]
**4. International Transfer --- No Transfer Impact Assessment (High)**

The DPA Template does not require, reference, or document any Transfer Impact Assessment for transfers to the United States (Transfer #2) or for remote access from Singapore (Transfer #3). Following the CJEU\'s *Schrems II* judgment (Case C-311/18) and EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 (Version 2.0), a TIA is a prerequisite for reliance on SCCs as a transfer mechanism. The TIA must assess US and Singaporean surveillance laws, the availability of effective legal remedies, and the necessity of supplementary measures. The DPA must require the completion and documentation of a TIA for each identified international transfer, with provisions for periodic reassessment as the legal landscape evolves. *See Diagram 3 (Section 3.3), Diagram 4 (Section 3.4), and Summary Table (Section 4).* \[References: \]
**5. Anonymization Standard Undefined (Medium-High)**

Orionis Analytics Ltd. provides \"anonymization and analytics\" services, but the DPA Template does not define anonymization or distinguish it from pseudonymization. If Orionis\'s outputs are pseudonymized rather than truly anonymized under the standard established in WP29 Opinion 05/2014 (WP216, endorsed by the EDPB), those outputs remain personal data under the GDPR and are subject to all DPA obligations. The DPA must: (a) define the anonymization standard by reference to the WP29/EDPB three-criteria test (singling out, linkability, inference); (b) require Orionis to validate and certify that its outputs satisfy the defined standard; (c) specify that outputs failing to meet the standard are treated as personal data subject to all DPA protections; and (d) address whether pre-anonymization analytics processing requires separate lawful basis documentation. *See Section 1.3.2, Diagram 5 (Section 3.5), and Summary Table (Section 4), Transfer #4.* \[References: \]

**Scope Limitation:** This document focuses exclusively on data flow mapping and international transfer mechanism issues. Additional compliance gaps related to HIPAA Business Associate Agreement integration, breach notification timelines and thresholds, liability cap structure and allocation, CCPA/CPRA Service Provider provisions, audit rights and frequency, data deletion and return procedures, governing law and dispute resolution, DPO coordination requirements, and contractual survival periods are addressed in the separate compliance gap memorandum being prepared concurrently by this office and outside counsel.

503: **B.1 Encryption. Encryption at Rest:** All Personal Data stored in the Processor\'s data centers, including data stored in databases, file systems, object storage, and backup media, is encrypted at rest using the Advanced Encryption Standard with 256-bit keys (AES-256). Encryption at rest is applied uniformly across all storage tiers and replication targets, including primary storage in Frankfurt, secondary storage in Dublin, and disaster recovery storage in Northern Virginia.
504: 
505: **Encryption in Transit:** All data transmissions involving Personal Data are encrypted in transit using Transport Layer Security version 1.3 (TLS 1.3) or higher. This includes transmissions between the Controller\'s systems and the Processor\'s cloud infrastructure, transmissions between the Processor\'s data centers (Frankfurt, Dublin, and Northern Virginia), and transmissions between the Processor and its Subprocessors. The Processor does not support deprecated encryption protocols (including SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1) for any connections involving Personal Data.
506: 
507: **Key Management:** Encryption keys are managed through a centralized key management system utilizing FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules (HSMs). Encryption keys are generated using cryptographically secure random number generators, stored in the HSMs, and rotated on an annual basis in accordance with the Processor\'s key rotation policy. Key access is restricted to authorized personnel on a strict need-to-know basis, with all key management operations logged and auditable.
508: 
509: **B.2 Access Controls**
510: 
511: **Role-Based Access Control (RBAC):** The Processor implements role-based access control with least-privilege principles for all systems that Process Personal Data. Access to Personal Data is granted only to those personnel whose roles require such access for the performance of the Services, and access privileges are limited to the minimum level necessary for the performance of the assigned role.
512: 
513: **Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA):** Multi-factor authentication is required for all administrative and privileged access to systems that Process Personal Data. MFA is enforced through hardware tokens or authenticator applications; SMS-based authentication is not permitted for privileged access.
514: 
515: **Segregation of Duties:** Critical Processing activities, including database administration, key management, and access provisioning, are subject to segregation of duties controls. No single individual has the ability to perform all steps of a critical operation without independent verification or approval.
516: 
517: **Access Reviews:** The Processor\'s information security team conducts formal access reviews on a quarterly basis to verify that access privileges remain appropriate and aligned with current role assignments. Access that is no longer required is promptly revoked. Access review results are documented and retained for a minimum of three (3) years.
518: 
519: **B.3 Network Security**
520: 
521: **Firewalls and Network Segmentation:** The Processor\'s data centers employ multi-layered firewall architectures with network segmentation between client environments, management networks, and public-facing services. Each client environment is logically isolated from other client environments and from the Processor\'s internal management infrastructure.
522: 
523: **Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS):** The Processor deploys intrusion detection and prevention systems across all network segments. IDS/IPS systems are monitored continuously (24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year) by the Processor\'s security operations center (SOC). Alerts are triaged and escalated in accordance with the Processor\'s incident response procedures.
524: 
525: **Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing:** Automated vulnerability scanning is performed on a monthly basis across all systems and network segments that Process Personal Data. Critical and high-severity vulnerabilities are remediated within fourteen (14) calendar days of identification; medium-severity vulnerabilities are remediated within thirty (30) calendar days. Annual penetration testing is conducted by an independent, qualified third-party information security firm. Penetration test findings are reported to the Processor\'s Chief Information Security Officer and tracked to remediation.
526: 
527: **DDoS Mitigation:** The Processor employs distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) mitigation services to protect its cloud infrastructure and the Controller\'s hosted applications from volumetric, protocol, and application-layer DDoS attacks.
528: 
529: **B.4 Physical Security**
530: 
531: **Data Center Security:** All data centers utilized by the Processor (including subprocessor-operated data centers in Dublin and Northern Virginia) are equipped with the following physical security controls:
532: 
533: > • 24/7 on-site security personnel
534: >
535: > • Closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveillance with a minimum of ninety (90) days of recorded footage retention
536: >
537: > • Biometric access controls (fingerprint or iris scan) at all entry points to data processing areas
538: >
539: > • Mantrap (airlock) entry systems at primary data center entrances
540: >
541: > • Visitor management procedures requiring escort by authorized personnel at all times
542: 
543: **Environmental Controls:** Data centers are equipped with:
544: 
545: > • Fire detection and suppression systems (pre-action dry pipe sprinkler systems and gas-based suppression for server rooms)
546: >
547: > • Climate control systems maintaining optimal temperature and humidity for computing equipment
548: >
549: > • Redundant power supply, including uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems and on-site diesel generators with a minimum of seventy-two (72) hours of fuel reserve
550: >
551: > • Redundant network connectivity from multiple independent telecommunications providers
552: 
553: **B.5 Data Center Locations**
554: 
555: The Processor\'s data processing infrastructure is distributed across the following data center locations:
556: 
557:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
558:   **Data Center**          **Location**                                  **Operator**                                 **Role**
559:   ------------------------ --------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
560:   Frankfurt, Germany       Frankfurt am Main, Hesse, Germany             Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH             Primary EU data center --- production environment, primary data storage
561:

563:

566:

568: 
569: **Geographic Redundancy:** Personal Data is replicated across geographically redundant data centers (Frankfurt, Dublin, and Northern Virginia) to ensure availability and resilience in the event of a localized outage, natural disaster, or other disruption affecting a single data center.
570:

The incident response plan addresses the identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review of security incidents, including Personal Data Breaches.

The incident response team includes representatives from information security, legal, operations, and communications functions.

The certification covers the Processor\'s information security management system as it applies to the provision of cloud hosting, managed database, and analytics services from the Processor\'s Frankfurt data center.

The SOC 2 Type II report is available to the Controller upon request, subject to the execution of a non-disclosure agreement where required by the Processor\'s auditor.

**Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing:** Automated vulnerability scanning is performed on a monthly basis across all systems and network segments that Process Personal Data. Critical and high-severity vulnerabilities are remediated within fourteen (14) calendar days of identification; medium-severity vulnerabilities are remediated within thirty (30) calendar days. Annual penetration testing is conducted by an independent, qualified third-party information security firm. Penetration test findings are reported to the Processor\'s Chief Information Security Officer and tracked to remediation.

**DDoS Mitigation:** The Processor employs distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) mitigation services to protect its cloud infrastructure and the Controller\'s hosted applications from volumetric, protocol, and application-layer DDoS attacks.
**B.4 Physical Security**

**Data Center Security:** All data centers utilized by the Processor (including subprocessor-operated data centers in Dublin and Northern Virginia) are equipped with the following physical security controls:
> • 24/7 on-site security personnel
> • Closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveillance with a minimum of ninety (90) days of recorded footage retention
> • Biometric access controls (fingerprint or iris scan) at all entry points to data processing areas
> • Mantrap (airlock) entry systems at primary data center entrances
> • Visitor management procedures requiring escort by authorized personnel at all times
**Environmental Controls:** Data centers are equipped with:
> • Fire detection and suppression systems (pre-action dry pipe sprinkler systems and gas-based suppression for server rooms)
> • Climate control systems maintaining optimal temperature and humidity for computing equipment
> • Redundant power supply, including uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems and on-site diesel generators with a minimum of seventy-two (72) hours of fuel reserve
> • Redundant network connectivity from multiple independent telecommunications providers
**B.5 Data Center Locations**
The Processor\'s data processing infrastructure is distributed across the following data center locations:
**Data Center**          **Location**                                  **Operator**                                 **Role**
Frankfurt, Germany       Frankfurt am Main, Hesse, Germany             Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH             Primary EU data center --- production environment, primary data storage
Dublin, Ireland          Dublin 2, Ireland                             Orionis Analytics Ltd. (Subprocessor)        Secondary EU data center --- anonymization and analytics processing
Northern Virginia, USA   Fairfax, Virginia, United States of America   Larkfield Data Systems, LLC (Subprocessor)   Disaster recovery data center --- database management, backup, and failover
**B.6 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery**

**Geographic Redundancy:** Personal Data is replicated across geographically redundant data centers (Frankfurt, Dublin, and Northern Virginia) to ensure availability and resilience in the event of a localized outage, natural disaster, or other disruption affecting a single data center.

**Recovery Point Objective (RPO):** The Processor maintains a recovery point objective of one (1) hour, meaning that in the event of a disaster or system failure, the maximum data loss shall not exceed one (1) hour of data.

**Recovery Time Objective (RTO):** The Processor maintains a recovery time objective of four (4) hours, meaning that in the event of a disaster or system failure affecting the primary production environment, the Processor targets restoration of Services within four (4) hours.

**Disaster Recovery Testing:** The Processor conducts comprehensive disaster recovery testing at least once per year, including simulated failover to the Northern Virginia disaster recovery site. Test results are documented and reviewed by the Processor\'s Chief Information Security Officer and Chief Technology Officer.
**B.7 Personnel Security**

**Background Checks:** All Processor personnel who have access to Personal Data are subject to background checks prior to commencing employment or engagement, including verification of identity, criminal records checks (to the extent permitted by applicable law), and verification of professional qualifications where relevant.
**Confidentiality Agreements:** All Processor personnel with access to Personal Data are required to execute written confidentiality agreements in accordance with Section 4 of the DPA.

**Security Awareness Training:** All Processor personnel receive annual security awareness training covering topics including data protection principles, information security policies and procedures, social engineering and phishing awareness, incident reporting procedures, and secure data handling practices. Training completion records are maintained by the Processor\'s human resources department.
**B.8 Incident Response**

**Incident Response Plan:** The Processor maintains a documented incident response plan that is reviewed and updated at least annually. The incident response plan addresses the identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review of security incidents, including Personal Data Breaches.

**Incident Response Team:** The Processor maintains a designated incident response team that is available twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a week, three hundred sixty-five (365) days a year. The incident response team includes representatives from information security, legal, operations, and communications functions.

**Alignment with ISO 27001:** The Processor\'s incident response procedures are aligned with the requirements of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, specifically Annex A Control A.5.24 (Information security incident management planning and preparation), A.5.25 (Assessment and decision on information security events), A.5.26 (Response to information security incidents), and A.5.27 (Learning from information security incidents).
**B.9 Certifications and Audits**

**ISO 27001:2022 Certification:** The Processor holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, Certificate Number ISO-27001-SC-2024-0891, issued by TÜV Rheinland AG on June 15, 2024, valid through June 14, 2027. The certification covers the Processor\'s information security management system as it applies to the provision of cloud hosting, managed database, and analytics services from the Processor\'s Frankfurt data center.

**SOC 2 Type II Report:** The Processor obtains an annual SOC 2 Type II report covering the Trust Services Criteria (Security, Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy). The most recent SOC 2 Type II report was dated September 30, 2024, covering the audit period from October 1, 2023 through September 30, 2024, and was issued by Clearwater Audit Partners GmbH. The SOC 2 Type II report is available to the Controller upon request, subject to the execution of a non-disclosure agreement where required by the Processor\'s auditor.

**Ongoing Compliance:** The Processor is committed to maintaining its ISO 27001 certification and obtaining annual SOC 2 Type II reports throughout the term of the DPA. The Processor shall promptly notify the Controller of any material findings, qualifications, or exceptions identified in any certification audit or SOC 2 examination that are relevant to the Processing of Personal Data on behalf of the Controller.
*End of Annex B --- Technical and Organizational Measures*
*--- End of Data Processing Agreement, Version 3.2 ---*
*Stratosphere Cloud Services GmbH*
*January 10, 2025*

{"command":"python - <<'PY'
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from docx.enum.text import WD_LINE_SPACING
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.enum.table import WD_ROW_HEIGHT_RULE
from docx.enum.text import WD_TAB_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.text import WD_TAB_LEADER
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE
from docx.shared import Cm

OUT = 'output/compliance-gap-memorandum.docx'

doc = Document()
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.top_margin = Inches(0.65)
sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.65)
sec.left_margin = Inches(0.72)
sec.right_margin = Inches(0.72)
sec.header_distance = Inches(0.25)
sec.footer_distance = Inches(0.25)

# Colors
NAVY = '17365D'
BLUE = '1F4E79'
LIGHT_BLUE = 'D9EAF7'
PALE_BLUE = 'EEF5FB'
RED = '9C0006'
PALE_RED = 'FCE4D6'
ORANGE = 'C65911'
PALE_ORANGE = 'FCE4D6'
GREEN = '006100'
PALE_GREEN = 'E2F0D9'
GRAY = '666666'
LIGHT_GRAY = 'F2F2F2'
DARK = '222222'

# Helpers
def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd')
        tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders')
        tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            edge_data = kwargs.get(edge)
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge)
            element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag)
                tcBorders.append(element)
            for key in ['val','sz','space','color']:
                if key in edge_data:
                    element.set(qn('w:{}'.format(key)), str(edge_data[key]))

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=90, bottom=80, end=90):
    tc = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
        tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top', top), ('start', start), ('bottom', bottom), ('end', end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn('w:'+m))
        if node is None:
            node = OxmlElement('w:'+m)
            tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v))
        node.set(qn('w:type'), 'dxa')

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader')
    tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'), 'true')
    trPr.append(tblHeader)

def set_keep_with_next(paragraph, val=True):
    pPr = paragraph._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    keep = pPr.find(qn('w:keepNext'))
    if val and keep is None:
        keep = OxmlElement('w:keepNext')
        pPr.append(keep)
    elif not val and keep is not None:
        pPr.remove(keep)

def shade_paragraph(paragraph, fill, border='B7C9D6'):
    p = paragraph._p
    pPr = p.get_or_add_pPr()
    shd = pPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); pPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)
    pBdr = pPr.find(qn('w:pBdr'))
    if pBdr is None:
        pBdr = OxmlElement('w:pBdr'); pPr.append(pBdr)
    left = OxmlElement('w:left')
    left.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); left.set(qn('w:sz'),'12'); left.set(qn('w:space'),'4'); left.set(qn('w:color'),border)
    pBdr.append(left)

def add_run(paragraph, text, bold=False, italic=False, color=None, size=None, underline=False):
    r = paragraph.add_run(text)
    r.bold = bold; r.italic = italic; r.underline = underline
    if color: r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(color)
    if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
    r.font.name = 'Aptos'
    r._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'), 'Aptos')
    return r

def add_p(text='', style=None, bold=False, italic=False, color=None, size=None, align=None, space_after=4, space_before=0, keep=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    if text:
        add_run(p, text, bold, italic, color, size)
    if align is not None: p.alignment = align
    pf = p.paragraph_format
    pf.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    pf.space_before = Pt(space_before)
    pf.line_spacing = 1.08
    if keep: set_keep_with_next(p)
    return p

def add_bullet(text, level=0, bold_prefix=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Bullet' if level==0 else 'List Bullet 2')
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05
    if bold_prefix and text.startswith(bold_prefix):
        add_run(p, bold_prefix, bold=True)
        add_run(p, text[len(bold_prefix):])
    else:
        add_run(p, text)
    return p

def add_numbered(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style='List Number')
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.05

The data-flow map identifies approximately 890,000 California residents, and both Stratosphere and Larkfield process the data. Flow the restrictions to Larkfield and any future subprocessor.','“Processor certifies that it understands and will comply with the following restrictions: it shall not sell or share Personal Information; retain, use or disclose it except to perform the Services and permitted business purposes; use it outside the direct business relationship; or combine it with information from other sources except as permitted by the CCPA/CPRA. Processor shall permit Controller to take reasonable steps to monitor compliance and shall promptly notify Controller if it can no longer comply.”','Playbook §7.1, Appendix B.4; data-flow §2.2.3; DPA §§1, 6.'),
('P1-07 — Breach notification timeline and content','HIGH / MUST-HAVE','DPA §9.1 provides 48 hours after the incident-response team or management confirms a GDPR Personal Data Breach. This is too late and too narrow: it omits reasonably suspected incidents, HIPAA Breaches of Unsecured PHI, California personal information incidents, the playbook’s discovery standard, direct Pinnacle contacts, and individual-identification information needed for notifications. The €1,000/day penalty is capped at €50,000, below the playbook preferred $5,000/day uncapped / fallback $2,500/day with a $250,000 minimum cap.','Replace §9.1 with 24 hours from discovery of an actual or reasonably suspected incident, regardless of confirmation. Add immediate phone and written notice to the CPO and Legal, required content, updates, cooperation and a penalty position. Make the incident definition encompass security incidents, GDPR breaches, HIPAA breaches and CCPA events.','“Processor shall notify Controller’s Chief Privacy Officer at privacy-incidents@pinnaclehealth.com and by telephone at (512) 555-0199, with a copy to legal-notices@pinnaclehealth.com, of any actual or reasonably suspected Security Incident, Personal Data Breach, or Breach of Unsecured PHI without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of discovery. Discovery means the first day known or reasonably knowable through diligence. Initial notice may be preliminary but must be supplemented as facts develop.”','Playbook §§5.1–5.3, Appendix B.2; DPA §9; email thread Apr. 16.'),
('P1-08 — Audit rights and HIPAA audit scope','HIGH / REDLINE','DPA §11.2 permits only one planned audit per year with 30 days’ notice; §11.3 limits it to Frankfurt; §11.4 lets Stratosphere satisfy the request with SOC 2/ISO materials. This excludes Dublin, Northern Virginia, backups and any subprocessor site, and provides no no-notice for-cause audit. It also lacks the required HIPAA review of risk assessments, workforce training, incident logs, PHI policies, Privacy/Security Officers and physical/technical safeguards.','Replace §11 with direct or third-party audit rights over all processing locations and subprocessors. Seek two audits/year (planned + for-cause, 15 days / no notice); fallback one planned audit with 30 days plus no-notice for cause. SOC 2/ISO must supplement, not replace, audit rights, and be provided within 30 days of request.','“Controller may audit Processor and each Subprocessor, including all data centers, DR/backup sites, policies, records, systems, personnel and HIPAA safeguards. Planned audits require 15 days’ notice; for-cause audits following an actual/suspected incident, regulatory inquiry or material concern may occur without notice. Processor shall contractually require equivalent audit access from each Subprocessor. SOC 2 and ISO materials supplement and do not replace these rights.”','Playbook §§8.1–8.2, Appendix B.5; DPA §§11.1–11.6; data-flow §1.2.'),
('P1-09 — Controller identity, definitions and processing schedule','HIGH / CORRECT BEFORE SIGNATURE','Annex A.1 leaves the Controller name, address, contact and activities blank. The MSA/data-flow documents two Controllers/entities: Pinnacle Health Solutions, Inc. for US services and Pinnacle Health Solutions EU B.V. for EU services. The template’s definitions are GDPR-only. This creates ambiguity over who gives instructions, who receives notices, who is the HIPAA Covered Entity, and who is the EU SCC beneficiary/exporter.','Name both entities and their roles, or identify the applicable controller by SOW and make the DPA expressly cover both. Add HIPAA and CCPA/CPRA definitions. Expand Annex A to include volumes, special-category data, PHI, California PI, purposes, locations, remote access, transfer paths, retention and authorized subprocessors.','“Controller means, as applicable, Pinnacle Health Solutions, Inc. for US Data and Pinnacle Health Solutions EU B.V. for EU/EEA Data, each acting within the role identified in the applicable SOW. Processor shall follow documented instructions from the applicable Controller and shall direct each notice to both Controllers where the event affects both data sets.”','Playbook §§3.1–3.2; DPA §§1–2 and Annex A.1–A.12; MSA §§1, 3, 9; data-flow §§1–2.'),
('P1-10 — Contractual DPO coordination protocol','HIGH / NEGOTIATION COMMITMENT','DPA §15 identifies Dr. Annika Vogt and promises a response within ten business days, but does not create a protocol for incident response, DPIAs, transfer assessments or supervisory-authority inquiries. The April 16–18 emails show this is a live negotiation point: Stratosphere prefers operational arrangements; Pinnacle has stated that board/compliance requirements make contractual coordination necessary.','Add a lean, operationally workable protocol: named contacts, 24/7 incident escalation, regulator/DPIA/TIA coordination, notice of DPO changes, reasonable response times, and a no-waiver statement preserving each party’s independent regulatory obligations.','“The parties shall maintain a documented privacy coordination protocol. Stratosphere’s DPO shall coordinate with Pinnacle’s CPO, Legal and EU privacy contacts for incidents, DPIAs, TIAs, data-subject requests and supervisory-authority inquiries. Incident coordination is 24/7; ordinary regulatory or DPIA requests receive an initial response within five business days and substantive assistance within ten business days, or sooner where a statutory deadline requires.”','Playbook §§14–15; DPA §§10, 15; email thread Apr. 16–18.'),
('P1-11 — Term and survival / HIPAA six-year protection','HIGH / MUST-HAVE','DPA §16.1 is generally coterminous with the MSA, which is positive, but §16.3 limits breach, audit, deletion and liability provisions to two years. It does not expressly preserve BAA obligations, HIPAA security/confidentiality/audit protections or retention-related obligations for six years. Section 16.4’s “applicable law” savings clause is not a substitute for clear contractual survival.','Retain coterminous term. Make breach, return/deletion, liability/indemnity, audit and confidentiality survive as necessary; make BAA/HIPAA obligations survive for six years from record creation/last effectiveness or as long as PHI is retained, whichever is longer.','“The BAA and all HIPAA-related privacy, security, confidentiality, audit, incident-response and record-retention obligations survive for six years from creation or last effectiveness of the applicable record, or for as long as Processor or a Subprocessor retains PHI, whichever is longer. General non-HIPAA survival may be two to three years only if it does not limit this carve-out.”','Playbook §§9.2, 15; DPA §16; MSA §§2, 11.'),
('P1-12 — Subprocessor flow-down and objection mechanics','HIGH / PARTIAL ALIGNMENT','DPA §6 has a current list, 15-day advance notice, an objection mechanism and full vendor liability. Those are useful and should be preserved. The gap is that “equivalent GDPR obligations” is not expressly stated to include HIPAA BAA duties, CCPA/CPRA Service Provider restrictions, transfer mechanisms/TIAs and all audit rights. The remedy is termination of affected Services only, after a 30-day negotiation and 60-day notice, rather than a clear no-penalty termination right if an objection is not resolved.','Add all-regime flow-down and require the current list to include data categories, exact locations, purpose, DPF status, transfer mechanism and certification scope. Seek 30 days’ objection window; preserve 15 days only as fallback. Permit termination of affected processing/DPA without penalty if the objection cannot be resolved.','“Processor shall impose on each Subprocessor obligations no less protective than this DPA, including the BAA, CCPA/CPRA restrictions, Article 28 terms, security, audit, breach, deletion and international-transfer/TIA obligations. Processor remains fully liable. Controller may object within 30 days; if unresolved before processing begins, Controller may terminate the affected Services without penalty.”','Playbook §§11–12; DPA §6; data-flow §§1.3, 4.'),
('P1-13 — Annex and security-scope accuracy','HIGH / VERIFY','The DPA contains strong baseline TOMs: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, RBAC/least privilege, MFA for privileged access, quarterly access reviews, monthly scanning, 14-day critical/high remediation, annual penetration testing, and ISO/SOC commitments. However, Annex B.5 identifies Dublin as operated by Orionis and calls it a secondary EU data center, while the MSA and data-flow map identify Dublin as a Stratosphere data center and Orionis as an analytics subprocessor. Annex B.9 says ISO certification covers Frankfurt only, while the MSA says Frankfurt and Dublin are in scope. Larkfield and Singapore coverage remains unconfirmed.','Retain the TOMs but correct the operator/location matrix. Require current ISO/SOC scope statements covering each location and service; if Larkfield or Singapore operations are outside scope, require equivalent evidence, contractual controls, and remediation. Add TLS 1.3 confirmation for Frankfurt→Northern Virginia DR and Frankfurt/Dublin→Orionis.','“Processor shall maintain an accurate processing-location and subprocessor schedule. No location or remote-access operation may be treated as within the certification scope unless the relevant certificate/report expressly covers it. Processor shall notify Controller of any scope exclusion or material qualification and provide equivalent controls and evidence within 30 days.”','Playbook §13; DPA §§5, 6, Annex B.1–B.9; MSA §§3, 10; data-flow §§1.2, 3.3, 3.5.'),
('P2-14 — Rights assistance and fee control','MEDIUM / CLOSE BEFORE SIGNATURE','DPA §8 is a relative strength: five-business-day direct-request notice is aligned with the playbook nice-to-have, and ten-business-day substantive help is within the fallback. It nevertheless addresses only GDPR rights and allows “reasonable fees” for material costs without defining ordinary compliance assistance. It does not expressly address HIPAA access, CCPA/CPRA rights to know/delete/correct/opt-out/limit, or confirmation of completion.','Extend assistance to HIPAA and CCPA/CPRA; require response within five business days where practicable and ten business days as fallback, with expedited handling for statutory deadlines. Exclude ordinary searches, exports, deletion/correction and compliance support from fees; require written approval before exceptional costs.','“Processor shall assist with GDPR, HIPAA and CCPA/CPRA requests, including search, access, export, correction, restriction, deletion, opt-out and confirmation. Assistance shall be provided within five business days where practicable and in all events within ten business days, or sooner where needed for Controller’s legal deadline. No additional fee applies to ordinary assistance required to comply with this DPA; exceptional costs require prior written approval.”','Playbook §14; DPA §8; data-flow §§2.1–2.2.'),
('P2-15 — DPIA/TIA support and documentation','MEDIUM / TIED TO P0-03','DPA §10 provides DPIA support but permits fees and a 20-business-day response. It does not require transfer impact assessments or periodic review. The EU patient data includes Article 9 health data processed at projected scale, so the data-flow document identifies a likely DPIA. The DPA should make vendor information and TIA support operationally usable within Pinnacle’s regulatory deadlines.','Add express TIA duty, cooperation, evidence delivery, legal-change updates and annual/triggered reassessment. Preserve a reasonable baseline of no-fee assistance for mandatory compliance documentation, with prior approval for genuinely extraordinary work.','“Processor shall promptly provide information and assistance reasonably required for Controller’s DPIA, prior consultation, TIA and regulatory compliance activities. Processor shall maintain a TIA for each third-country transfer, update it at least annually and upon material legal or processing change, and provide it on request. Ordinary assistance required by this DPA is included in the Services.”','Playbook §§11.1, 13.1, 14; DPA §§7, 10; data-flow §§2.1, 3.3–3.5.')
]

add_heading('Detailed Findings and Redline Recommendations', 1)
for title, priority, assessment, redline, clause, source in findings:
    add_heading(title, 2)
    p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(3); p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next=True

# positives

add_p('The redline should not unnecessarily reopen provisions that already track the playbook or provide a useful baseline. Preserve these terms while extending them to the US and all processing locations:')
for t in [

    '§5 TOMs: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, RBAC, MFA for privileged access, quarterly access review, network segmentation, IDS/IPS, monthly vulnerability scanning, 14-day critical/high remediation and annual penetration testing.',
    '§6 current identification of Larkfield and Orionis, 15-day notice as a fallback-acceptable objection window, written subprocessor flow-down and Stratosphere’s express full liability for subprocessors. Add the missing HIPAA/CCPA/transfer terms rather than removing these protections.',
    '§8 five-business-day notification if a data subject contacts the processor and ten-business-day substantive assistance, subject to extending the scope to HIPAA/CCPA and controlling fees.',
    '§10 DPIA assistance, §15 named DPO, and §16.1 coterminous term with the MSA; these are good foundations for the revised coordination and survival provisions.'
]: add_bullet(t)

# negotiation roadmap
add_heading('Recommended Negotiation Sequence', 1)
roadmap = [

('2. Resolve gating terms first','At the April 30 call / first substantive session, address BAA execution, liability structure, transfer mechanisms/TIAs, US law/forum and data return. These are the matters most likely to affect the September 1 launch.'),
('3. Close regulatory schedules','Exchange a completed Annex A / processing schedule, CCPA addendum, BAA, SCC Module 3 for Larkfield and a Singapore access decision. Require written confirmation of Larkfield’s DPF status and certification/report scope.'),
('4. Verify operations','Obtain current SOC 2 and ISO scope statements; validate that Larkfield/Northern Virginia and Singapore access are covered or subject to equivalent controls. Confirm TLS 1.3 for the DR transfer and the operator identity for Dublin.'),
('5. Escalate as required','If Stratosphere maintains €500,000, refuses the BAA or CCPA certification, refuses subprocessor audits, insists on non-US law/forum for US data or refuses data return, document the position and escalate immediately to Margaret Yuen-Park and Rachel Osterfeld. Do not make an unapproved concession.'),
('6. Sign only after checklist completion','Do not execute Exhibit D or permit EU Services to go live until the DPA, BAA, CCPA terms, SCC modules, TIAs, corrected schedules and signature blocks are complete and internally approved.')
]
add_table(['Step','Action'], roadmap,[1.35,5.15],font_size=8.3)

# appendix issue checklist

('☐','BAA / PHI','Executed integrated BAA or Exhibit E; definitions; permitted uses; minimum necessary; safeguards; training; breach; subcontractor flow-down; six-year records; return/destruction.'),
('☐','CCPA/CPRA','Integrated terms or addendum; no sell/share; purpose/direct relationship; no combining; certification; monitoring; inability-to-comply notice; consumer-rights assistance.'),
('☐','Transfers','Module 3 with Larkfield; Module 2 only where appropriate; Singapore path resolved; TIA for each third-country path; supplementary measures; periodic reassessment.'),
('☐','Liability','2x cap floor ($8.4M combined); regional floor where applicable; uncapped carve-outs; indemnity; consequential-damages qualification.'),

('☐','Forum','US: Delaware law + W.D. Texas / Travis County courts; EU: Netherlands (German fallback) + DIS/ICC/LCIA arbitration.'),

]

**Considering data center discrepancies**

I see that there's a discrepancy regarding the Dublin data center. "Annex B lists Dublin as Orionis-operated," but the MSA/dataflow suggests Stratosphere owns it. This should definitely be addressed. It might be best to categorize this as a separate finding, maybe under finding 13, which deals with the integrity of annex and processing descriptions. It’s important to correct these inaccuracies to maintain clarity and reliability in the documentation.
